title: Memory Access Sizes [mov byte/word/dword/qword]
description:
## Specifying Size
When reading or writing memory, you must tell the CPU how many bytes to access:

```asm
mov byte  [rdi], 42      ; write 1 byte
mov word  [rdi], 1000    ; write 2 bytes
mov dword [rdi], 100000  ; write 4 bytes
mov qword [rdi], rax     ; write 8 bytes
```

Without the size, NASM doesn't know how many bytes you mean:
```asm
mov [rdi], 42   ; ERROR! ambiguous size
```

### Matching registers to sizes:
| Size | Register | Keyword |
|------|----------|---------|
| 1 byte | al, bl, cl, dl | `byte` |
| 2 bytes | ax, bx, cx, dx | `word` |
| 4 bytes | eax, ebx, ecx, edx | `dword` |
| 8 bytes | rax, rbx, rcx, rdx | `qword` |

When using a full register, the size is implied:
```asm
mov [rdi], eax   ; 4 bytes (eax is 32-bit)
mov [rdi], rax   ; 8 bytes (rax is 64-bit)
```

---
## Assignment:
LHINX stores mixed-size config data. Write a function `read_config` that takes a pointer in `rdi` to this layout:
- Byte 0: version (1 byte)
- Bytes 1-2: flags (2 bytes)
- Bytes 3-6: uptime (4 bytes)

Return `version + flags + uptime` in `rax`.
setupCode:
section .data
    s_pass db "Pass", 10
    s_pass_len equ $ - s_pass
    s_fail db "Fail", 10
    s_fail_len equ $ - s_fail
    s_PASS db "---------------------", 10, "PASS", 10
    s_PASS_len equ $ - s_PASS
    s_FAIL db "---------------------", 10, "FAIL", 10
    s_FAIL_len equ $ - s_FAIL
    s_div db "---------------------", 10
    s_div_len equ $ - s_div
    config1:
        db 1
        dw 10
        dd 1000
    config2:
        db 5
        dw 100
        dd 50000

section .text
    global _start
starterCode:
read_config:
    ; rdi = pointer to config
    ; return version + flags + uptime in rax
    ret
runHarness:
_start:
    xor r12, r12

    ; print divider
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_div
    mov rdx, s_div_len
    syscall

    ; test 1
    lea rdi, [config1]
    call read_config
    cmp rax, 1011
    je .p1
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_fail
    mov rdx, s_fail_len
    syscall
    jmp .t2
.p1:
    inc r12
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_pass
    mov rdx, s_pass_len
    syscall
.t2:
    ; print divider
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_div
    mov rdx, s_div_len
    syscall

    ; test 2
    lea rdi, [config2]
    call read_config
    cmp rax, 50105
    je .p2
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_fail
    mov rdx, s_fail_len
    syscall
    jmp .done
.p2:
    inc r12
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_pass
    mov rdx, s_pass_len
    syscall
.done:
    cmp r12, 2
    je .allpass
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_FAIL
    mov rdx, s_FAIL_len
    syscall
    jmp .exit
.allpass:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, s_PASS
    mov rdx, s_PASS_len
    syscall
.exit:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hint: Use movzx to zero-extend smaller values into 64-bit registers. movzx rax, byte [rdi] for the version, movzx rbx, word [rdi+1] for flags, mov ecx, [rdi+3] for uptime. Then add them.
